narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which estimated an 81% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — a high enough likelihood that your application was unfortunately denied. This means the model found your current financial profile to be significantly more similar to applicants who have struggled to repay loans than to those who have successfully done so. Understanding why this happened, and what could change the outcome, is important for your next steps.

To help explain this decision, we can look at "what if" scenarios — alternative versions of your profile that would have led to an approval. These counterfactual scenarios show the minimum changes needed to flip the model's assessment from "bad credit risk" to "good credit." In your case, the analysis generated one such scenario, and it points to a single, very specific factor as the decisive issue.

The one change that would flip the model's decision is your credit history. Currently, your credit history is recorded as "no credits/all paid," which sounds positive on the surface but is actually interpreted cautiously by the model — it means there is very little evidence of how you handle ongoing credit obligations. Among approved applicants, only about 2.3% share this credit history category, making it one of the rarest profiles among those who were approved. By contrast, the vast majority of approved applicants — over 85% — have a history of either existing paid credits or critical/other credits, meaning they have demonstrably managed credit accounts over time. The counterfactual scenario shows that if your credit history were instead categorized as "critical/other existing credits," the model would approve your application, with everything else about your profile remaining exactly the same.

It is worth noting that several aspects of your profile are actually quite favorable. Your requested loan amount of 1,082 DM is well below the average of approximately 2,887 DM among approved applicants, meaning you are asking for considerably less than most. Your loan duration of 12 months is also shorter than the approved applicant average of about 19 months, which typically signals lower risk. You own your home, have stable employment of 1 to 4 years, and your purpose — purchasing a new car — is a common and accepted reason for borrowing. None of these factors needed to change in the counterfactual scenario, which confirms they are not working against you.

The core challenge is that the model has very little evidence of your track record with credit. The most actionable path forward would be to build a demonstrable credit history — for example, by taking out and successfully repaying a smaller credit product, such as a store installment plan or a small personal loan, before reapplying. Over time, having active and well-managed credit accounts on record would shift your credit history into a category that the model views far more favorably, and given how strong the rest of your profile already is, that single change appears to be all that stands between you and an approved application.
